resources.string: Menu or race?\nRacing controls appear while you drive and hide in menus. The layout switches automatically.

How do the menus work?\nIn Controls → Touch, choose Direct touch to tap menu items, or Touchpad to move the cursor by sliding. The Android Back button or gesture goes back. The keyboard opens when the game asks for text; Back closes it.

What does size change?\nButton size scales the default controls. In Edit positions & sizes, drag a control and move the Button slider to resize it; a control answers to touches exactly where it is drawn, and percentages are relative to the default control. Changes save automatically. The editor shows a grid; with Snap to grid on, a dragged control lands on it.
Edges and vertical position\nDistance from edges moves default controls inward. System cutouts are respected. Manually placed controls keep their saved positions.

Opacity and auto-hide\nOpacity sets normal visibility. Auto-hide starts after all fingers lift, after a delay of 1–30 seconds. Hidden buttons still respond on the first touch and become visible again. Holding a control prevents hiding. A press on player 1\'s pad hides the controls at once; the next touch brings them back. Player 2\'s pad leaves them alone, so one player can drive on the screen while the other plays on a pad.

Vibration\nThe game\'s Force Feedback effects are felt on the phone or on Gamepad 1, never on both at once: choose Off, Phone or Gamepad in Controls → Force Feedback. The game drives only one force-feedback device, so Gamepad 2 never vibrates. A gamepad\'s strength is set in the game itself: Options → Controllers → Force Feedback. Effects come from the game, never from button taps.

Display and game files\nDisplay controls screen orientation and the frame rate limit. A lower limit may reduce power use. Files & backups manages imported game files, saved games and launcher settings backups. Select active game files before playing.

Gamepads\nIn Controls → Gamepads, choose a controller for each player, test input and change menu controls. Automatic uses the remaining controllers in connection order. Saved player assignments stay reserved while their controllers are disconnected. Assign racing controls inside the game. If your menu Back button is assigned to racing, set a Race pause shortcut to pause by holding Back and an extra button.
Lights and recovery\n☼ switches the headlights. ↻ returns the car to the track. These on-screen buttons follow the corresponding assignments in the game’s Controls menu.
